messages:
Aisha: Heads up — after the driver v2.7.3 rollout last night I'm seeing a perf regression on the seqlen=128 path for aarch64 nodes. P95 up ~8%. Put quick repro below, logs attached to the thread :eyes:

Ben: Can you paste the repro and the top-level perf numbers?

Aisha: Sure — quick repro (local dev container against staging runtime):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/run \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rw-13b","input_len":128,"batch":4}'
```
Small perf diff snapshot (avg over 2k requests):
- x86_64 (before): p50=42ms, p95=120ms, tokens/s=950
- aarch64 (before): p50=45ms, p95=130ms, tokens/s=920
- aarch64 (after driver 2.7.3): p50=46ms, p95=140ms, tokens/s=850

Logs show the kernel selector switching from `attn-arch-optimized-v3` -> `attn-generic-v1` on aarch64. Also kvcache miss rate spiked ~+12% at the same time.

Carla: That kernel name swap smells like capability metadata changed in the driver handshake. We added a new `hw_features` blob in 2.7.x — if the selector logic treats unknown features as "incompatible" it may fall back to generic kernels.

Derek: +1. I was profiling the KV cache yesterday and saw a concurrent eviction surge during model reloads. If kernel mapping changes we may be producing different cache keys (or salt) which leads to mass misses.

Aisha: Confirmed in logs: when the driver restarted it emitted a different `kernel_map` fingerprint for the same model+arch. kvcache keys include kernel hints right now. That explains both kernel choice and miss spike.

Ben: Short-term mitigation idea: keep a stable mapping for a model_id -> kernel choice pinned by model_version until the runtime selector itself is patched. This avoids churn during driver rollouts. Proposed config flag: `kernel_reconciler.prefer_stable_mapping=true`.

Carla: Agree. Also we should add an explicit `kernel_map_v` field that the driver and runtime exchange so keying can be made explicit instead of implicit. Example key format we can standardize on:
```text
kvcache::{model_id}:{model_version}:{arch}:{kernel_map_v}:{input_prefix_hash}
```
That way when driver updates produce incompatible mappings we increment `kernel_map_v` and we can tombstone previous keys or accept misses intentionally.

Derek: We need a formal invalidation protocol when `kernel_map_v` increments. Proposal: driver emits `kernel_map_v` on startup; runtime persists last-seen `kernel_map_v` per model, and if new > old -> enqueue namespace purge for `kernel_map_v`-dependent keys (non-blocking) + increment metric `kvcache.invalidation_count`. Command for ops to purge quickly:
```bash
kvctl purge --namespace=model:{model_id} --match "kernel_map_v < {new_v}"
```

Lin: Ops question — can we rollback driver v2.7.3 while patch goes in? There's a small window where customers on aarch64 see higher P95s. If we pin stable mappings it's lower risk but rollback might be fastest.

deploy-bot: Deploy created: hotfix/kernel-reconciler-pin -> staging (PR #4521). CI triggered. :rocket:

Ben: Long-term: let's add a reconciler component that computes a deterministic kernel mapping given `(model_id, model_version, arch, hw_features)` and publishes a `kernel_map_v` hash. Runtime uses that stable mapping rather than ad-hoc selection rules. On driver schema changes, the reconciler can detect incompatible changes and bump `kernel_map_v` automatically.

Carla: Also add unit/integration tests: `eng-runtime/tests/test_kernel_map_rollforward.py` to cover driver schema bump, model reload, and kvcache churn.

Aisha: I'll open the reconciler PR with the pin config and the test, assign to @Ben and @Carla for review. I'll include the quick perf harness. CC @Lin for deploy window.

Ben: On it — running full perf suite on aarch64 farm now, will report numbers.

Lin: Scheduling a 02:00 UTC patch window; ops will standby.

Derek: After we stabilize keying we should measure the delta for seqlen=32/64/128 since kernel selection is sequence-length-dependent — might be that only certain bins are affected.

Aisha: Good call. Initial sampling shows seqlen=512 unaffected (same kernel), seqlen=128 hit the fallback. Will include per-bin breakdown in PR. :thumbsup:

Carla: One more note — add `kernel_map_v` to the model metadata snapshot stored with saved KV page cache so when we restore a warm cache after a restart we can verify version match and avoid silent mismatches.

Ben: ACK. I'll add migration code to mark cached pages with `kernel_map_v` meta and a background scanner that verifies versions on startup.

Lin: Thanks team. If PR goes green we'll promote to canary and watch `kvcache.hit_rate` + `p95` for seqlen 128 on aarch64.

Aisha: Thanks all — opening PR now.
